introduction: For the past six years, my academic and applied research has focused on gathering, cleaning, analysing, and modelling structured and unstructured data across media, migration, and international development.

I am now transitioning into commercial data analysis, leveraging my experience in defining key questions, validating data integrity, testing hypotheses, and effectively communicating findings. To facilitate this transition, I recently completed a government-funded Data and AI automation bootcamp with The Development Manager and developed the independent projects detailed below, using publicly available data from UK organisations.
opening: I am drawn to the stories behind quantitative data. My journey began in Nigeria, where I studied how rainfall affects rice farms. Since then, I have interviewed newspaper readers, investigated why skilled Nigerians emigrate to the UK, and experimented with artificial intelligence to analyse data more deeply. I'm now looking to apply my experience in a corporate data role.

milestones.title: I learned to think like a geographer.
milestones.text: I graduated top of my geography class at Ahmadu Bello University with first-class honours and straight As in statistics. My final project mapped rainfall variability and rice yields in a Nigerian local government area, connecting quantitative analysis with local context.
milestones.note: Geography taught me that context is crucial; a seemingly healthy average can mask significant local disparities.

milestones.title: I received a Chevening Scholarship and graduated with distinction.
milestones.text: A Chevening Scholarship funded my MSc in Conflict, Statebuilding and Development at the University of Birmingham. I analysed newspaper coverage and interviewed readers to explore framing effects. I graduated with distinction, scoring 82% in my dissertation.
milestones.note: Chevening: the UK government’s highly competitive scholarship programme for future leaders worldwide.

milestones.title: I trained in qualitative and quantitative research design and analysis.
milestones.text: ESRC funding supported my MA in Social Research at the University of Birmingham. I trained in qualitative and quantitative research design and analysis, including regression modelling, interviews and qualitative coding. I scored 75% in the quantitative module.
milestones.note: To find a good answer, first define the evidence you need. Let that decision guide data collection.

milestones.title: I started my PhD.
milestones.text: I started my PhD in International Development at the University of Birmingham with ESRC funding. I analysed nearly 29,000 posts on X and conducted interviews about skilled Nigerians’ migration to the UK, using Python and language models to examine textual data.
milestones.note: Online posts and personal conversations offer different perspectives. Effective social listening needs both, with their context intact.

milestones.title: I trained in LLMs and evaluated AI-assisted analysis.
milestones.text: At the University of Oxford’s Spring School in Large Language Models, I studied LLM architecture, configuration and evaluation. I compared AI and human text coding in my research, investigated disagreements and checked whether the coding scheme measured the intended concepts.
milestones.note: AI can accelerate analysis, but human oversight is necessary to identify and correct its errors.

milestones.title: I completed data and AI training and built business analytics projects.
milestones.text: I completed The Development Manager’s government-funded Data and AI Automation bootcamp. Alongside this transition, I learned SQL for a council payments project and analysed public UK organisational data. These four projects connect business questions with evidence and recommendations.
milestones.note: The core skills remain the same, but the application is new.

ending.heading: What this means for you
ending.lead: You’d get an analyst who prioritises understanding context and stakeholders over simply focusing on metrics.
points: I’ll disaggregate average figures by region, branch, product or customer group to identify underlying variations before identifying a trend.
I’ll cross-reference quantitative findings with qualitative feedback from customers.
I’ll leverage AI and automation for efficiency gains, while maintaining human oversight to mitigate potential errors.
I’ll present my findings and actionable recommendations in clear, accessible language.

additional_experience: My freelance experience also includes work with Outlier.
